title: Kuro, Eric and Mio as vinyl chibis, with Meshy
question: These are real 3D models (Meshy, rigged), not just pictures. The images below are renders of the models from several angles. Open the live 3D link to turn them and watch them idle and walk. They are now in the game: Eric, Mio and Kuro use them by default. Which of these work, and what should change?

media.caption: Your brief: "Now try making kuro, eric and mio in that style" (this is the Meshy side; another agent builds them by hand in Blender). Kuro: your picture, the input picture, then front, her left 3/4 (image right side turned to us), her left side and back. Same Blender camera and soft light as chibi-meshy-1.
Eric, same layout. His ponytail is missing at the back on both: the input is a front view, so Meshy never saw it.
Mio, same layout. mio-1 and mio-2 turned the messy bun into thin curled strands; mio-3 has a smooth round bun on her left (image right), as in her portrait.

Faces close up: your picture, then per attempt the input face and the model's face, front and left 3/4. The eyes stay crisp, flat and painted on every model. Glasses: Meshy built every pair as a real 3D frame standing off the face, thin silver for Eric, thick black for Kuro, taupe for Mio. On some it also painted a faint copy of the frame onto the skin (eric-1 beside his left eye, mio-1 and mio-2 under the lenses).

kuro-1 rigged (Meshy auto-rig on a copy decimated to 60,000 faces), in the live viewer with the game idle and walk. The walk is Mio's clip with the leg swing scaled to 0.55 for the short legs. The head still leans forward in the side view, as in chibi-meshy-1.

Every input picture for Kuro, in order (FLUX.2 Klein 4B on the local GPU, 4 steps, seeds 101 to 103). Image 1 is your office woman picture, so the figure, head, mitten hands and vinyl look come from it. Image 2 is her approved portrait. a: first prompt. b: the proportions spelled out in words (no visible change). c: started from your picture instead of noise, at denoise 0.9 (it carried your brown bob over, so I dropped it). d: "black hair with a dark blue sheen" instead of "blue-black", which had come out navy. kuro-d-101 went to Meshy. The lower body (pencil skirt, flats) is my choice; her portrait stops at the waist.

Every input picture for Eric. a to c as for Kuro. d: "dark golden blond" instead of "dark-blond", which came out brown. e: "large blue anime eyes as big as the woman's in image 1", since his eyes were small and narrow. f: the glasses asked for as "painted flat on the face like the eyes, with no 3D frame". The picture barely changed. eric-e-101 and eric-f-101 went to Meshy.

Every input picture for Mio. a to c as for Kuro. d: "near-black dark teal hoodie" instead of "very dark green", which came out mid green. f: "a smooth round bun" instead of "a messy bun", after Meshy turned the messy bun into strands; the bun hid behind her head on every seed. g: the bun placed "high at the back of her head on her left side, showing beside her head". g-101 had it on her right, so I mirrored the picture (mio-g-101-flip). mio-d-101 and mio-g-101-flip went to Meshy.

options.label: 1. kuro-1
options.note: Input kuro-d-101, background cut away (BiRefNet, CPU). Meshy image-to-3D with the settings of chibi-meshy-1's dressed-nopose: latest model, textured in the same task, no remesh, image enhancement off, no PBR, 4k texture, no pose. 30 credits, 411,354 triangles. Close to the input: bun with two hair sticks, blunt fringe, side locks, black frames, dark lips, teal blazer, skirt, flats, mitten hands. The hair sticks are thin rods. Rigged (5 credits): in the live viewer.

options.label: 2. eric-1
options.note: Input eric-e-101, same settings as 1. 30 credits, 445,636 triangles. Blond swept-back hair, stubble, silver frame, grey hoodie under a navy blazer, grey trousers. No ponytail (not in the front picture). His hands are rounder fists than the women's mittens. A faint second frame is painted on the skin beside his left eye. Rigged (5 credits): in the live viewer.

options.label: 3. mio-1
options.note: Input mio-d-101, same settings as 1. 30 credits, 760,332 triangles. Green-black hair with green streaks, taupe frames, pale skin, dark teal hoodie, cargo trousers. The messy bun came out as thin curled strands, and a faint copy of the frame is painted under the lenses. Rigged (5 credits): in the live viewer.

options.label: 4. kuro-2
options.note: 1 with one change: Meshy Smart Topology (meshy-t2, target 5,000 faces) instead of the latest model, for a game-light model. 15 credits, 5,377 triangles. Shape kept. The face texture is blotchier (grey patches on the cheeks) and the lenses look glassy. Not rigged.

options.label: 5. mio-2
options.note: 3 with one change: Smart Topology (meshy-t2, 5,000 faces), to see whether low poly turns the bun's strands into chunks. It didn't: the bun is still spiky strands with green bands. 15 credits, 5,287 triangles. Not rigged.

options.label: 6. eric-2
options.note: 2 with one change: input eric-f-101, glasses asked for as painted on. The picture barely changed, and Meshy still built a separate 3D frame. Otherwise as eric-1, without the painted second frame. 30 credits, 431,200 triangles. Not rigged.

options.label: 7. mio-3
options.note: 3 with a new input, mio-g-101-flip (smooth round bun on her left, image right), same Meshy settings. 30 credits, 567,130 triangles. The bun is now one clean ball. Fringe, streaks, frames and hoodie as before. Rigged (5 credits): in the live viewer.

links.label: Turn kuro-1, eric-1 and mio-3 (and mio-1), play the game idle and the shorter-step walk, side by side (live 3D)
Credits spent: Meshy 200 (five latest-model generations 150, two Smart Topology 30, four rigs 20), balance 1,085
Every input picture's prompt, seed and settings

decision: Decided 2026-10-03: Meshy chibis for everyone ("The meshy ones are much better. So just build on that and add them to the game"); kuro-1, eric-1, mio-3 are in the game (now the default look).
